headline: BARRICK FILES S-1 TO LIST US GOLD UNIT — American Barrick Gold (ABGC) Targets $62B Valuation on Nevada Gold Mines + Pueblo Viejo; Q4 2026 or Early 2027 IPO
snippet: Barrick Mining filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a US-listed spinoff called American Barrick Gold Corporation (NYSE target: ABGC), bundling its Nevada Gold Mines JV (61.5% stake alongside Newmont) and Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic (60%) into a standalone NYSE vehicle. Bloomberg Intelligence pegs the implied valuation at approximately US$62 billion. Mark Hill is named CEO. Barrick retains majority voting control and a US$1.2 billion annual dividend stream from the new entity; Newmont consented in exchange for a stake in the Fourmile project. The IPO is targeted for Q4 2026 or early 2027 and would rank among the largest mining listings in US history.

headline: COPPER TESTS $6/LB AS AI ROUT DEEPENS — LME Stocks Hit 328,000t, 200-Day MA Breaks; Uranium Holds $91/lb as Lithium Faces $12,000/t Citi Forecast
snippet: FX Empire's November 16 metals price analysis shows copper breaking below its 200-day moving average and testing the US$6 per pound psychological floor as the Nvidia CEO departure amplifies AI-sector uncertainty and risk-off sentiment sweeps base metals. LME copper warehouse stocks jumped to 328,000 tonnes, adding further pressure to a contract already down sharply from its 2026 highs. In contrast, uranium is holding near US$91.85 per pound while Citi has cut its lithium carbonate forecast to US$12,000 per tonne — marking a stark divergence between energy transition metals that depend on EV demand sentiment and those tied to AI power and nuclear utility contracting.

headline: CAN FALLING OIL RESCUE GOLD? — Brent's $20/BBL DROP FROM OCT PEAK CUTS MINING COSTS $22/OZ; Morgan Stanley's $5,200 TARGET DEPENDS ON IT
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's mid-November analysis frames the gold recovery thesis around a macro tailwind that most investors are overlooking: Brent crude's nearly US$20 per barrel decline from its October 30 peak of US$117.60 to around US$98.30 on November 10 reduces all-in sustaining costs by roughly US$22 per ounce — energy is about 12% of miners' cost structure at US$11 per ounce per US$10 per barrel. The piece argues Morgan Stanley's US$5,200 gold target is conditional on oil deflating further, and flags that Tuesday's US retail sales and Wednesday's FOMC minutes are the key binary catalysts this week before any seasonal Q4 gold rally can materialise.

headline: EVEN AT $4,000 GOLD, MAJOR PRODUCERS ARE FINE — Newmont AISC $1,545, Barrick Below $1,950; Sector at 0.74x NAV vs. 0.91x Historical Average
snippet: Crux Investor's latest analysis cuts through the gold equity panic by mapping actual all-in sustaining costs against the feared downside scenario: Newmont guided 2026 AISC at US$1,545 per ounce, Barrick at US$1,760–$1,950, implying margins above US$1,900–$2,300 per ounce even at a US$3,879 gold price. The sector is currently trading at 0.74x net asset value versus a historical average of 0.91x — a 20% discount that has historically resolved in favour of the equity, not the metal. The piece argues the selloff has priced in a scenario that is both arithmetically unlikely (gold below mining costs) and structurally unsupported (physical demand, central bank buying, and ETF outflows that have already plateaued).

headline: PERU RAISES THE BAR FOR COPPER EXPLORERS — New 60-Platform DIA Threshold Shortens Junior Drilling Timelines vs. Colombia; Jurisdiction Risk Framework for TSX-V
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis maps the regulatory divergence between Peru and Colombia for TSX-V copper explorers deciding where to deploy capital. Peru raised its environmental impact declaration threshold from 40 to 60 drill platforms in 2026, reducing the filing burden and potentially shortening junior exploration timelines for mid-sized programs. The piece provides a comparative risk framework covering permitting timelines, community engagement requirements, infrastructure access, and country risk, and assesses the practical consequences for copper explorers choosing between the two key South American jurisdictions in the current financing environment.

headline: SILVER FACES SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT YEAR — Stock DRAWDOWN Now Raising Physical SQUEEZE Risks as ETF Outflows and Price Weakness Mask Structural Shortage
snippet: Fresh research ahead of the Silver Institute's mid-November 2026 interim review shows silver is heading for a sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces, with accumulated stock drawdowns now approaching a level where identifiable inventory is insufficient to satisfy a demand surge. The paradox: spot silver at multi-year lows near US$47 coincides with the tightest-ever multi-year deficit run on record. Industrial offtake from photovoltaics — roughly 232 million ounces annually — is not responding to price weakness, while investment outflows triggered by US dollar strength and rising real rates have driven the selloff. The growing gap between paper price and physical reality is the central squeeze risk for the near term.

headline: THESE AUSTRALIAN JUNIORS DEFIED THE 2026 BEAR MARKET — BOA Resources, Peers Post Drill Hits Amid Sector-Wide Selloff
snippet: Stockhead identifies a cohort of Australian small-cap miners that have held up or advanced during 2026's sector-wide correction, with BOA Resources returning 14 metres at 2.49% copper as one of the standout performers. The piece profiles the characteristics that separated resilient juniors from the broader selloff — funded programs, high-grade discovery holes, and projects in provinces where infrastructure reduces development risk — and argues that the current environment has created a rare bifurcation where exploration-stage companies with genuine geological news are trading at multi-year relative value premiums to producers.

headline: FRANCE OPENS EUROPE'S FIRST LARGE-SCALE BATTERY BLACK MASS PLANT — Veolia's 7,000t/Year Facility Recovers 90%+ Cobalt, Nickel and Copper From End-of-Life EV Batteries
snippet: Veolia has opened a French processing facility capable of handling 7,000 tonnes of battery black mass per year — the product of shredded end-of-life lithium-ion batteries — recovering more than 90% of the cobalt, nickel, and copper content for reuse in new battery manufacturing. The plant represents a significant step toward closing the European battery recycling loop at scale, reducing dependence on primary mine supply for critical battery metals at a time when lithium carbonate prices face bearish forecasts and new mine supply from Australia and South America is hitting the market. It is the first facility of this scale in Western Europe.

headline: UZBEKISTAN TO DOUBLE URANIUM OUTPUT BY 2030 — Navoiyuran Plans 15,000t/Year vs. 7,500t Today; Major New Supply Entering a Market Priced at $91.85/lb
snippet: Uzbekistan's state uranium producer Navoiyuran has announced plans to double production from approximately 7,500 tonnes per year in 2026 to 15,000 tonnes by 2030, representing a potential addition of roughly 7,500 tonnes to global uranium supply — equivalent to about 15% of current annual mine production. The announcement comes as spot uranium holds near US$91.85 per pound on strong utility contracting and AI data centre power demand, and raises a supply question that the uranium bull case has largely sidestepped: whether incremental ISL output from Central Asia can close the structural gap between mine production and reactor demand without triggering a material price correction.

headline: CAN KINROSS SUSTAIN Q4 MARGIN MOMENTUM? — Gold's Seasonal Setup Historically Strong; AISC Below $1,600 Puts KGC Among Best-Levered Producers in a Recovery
snippet: Zacks examines whether Kinross Gold (NYSE: KGC) can carry its strong Q3 margin performance into Q4 as gold enters what is historically its most seasonally favourable quarter. With all-in sustaining costs guidance tracking below US$1,600 per ounce, Kinross sits at the lower end of the major producer cost curve — giving it both margin protection if gold stays near US$3,879 and outsized upside if Q4 seasonality and the FOMC-data binary this week resolve in favour of a precious metals recovery. The analysis flags Kinross's leverage to any gold price recovery as among the best in the large-cap producer space.

headline: SILVER'S DEMAND DRIVER IS SHIFTING — Solar Substitution Erodes PV Offtake as AI and EV Applications Absorb the Shortfall; New Structural Demand Mix Changes the Deficit Math
snippet: Crux Investor's November analysis documents the demand-driver rotation in silver: solar panel manufacturers are increasingly substituting away from silver contacts to reduce costs, shaving an estimated 15–20 million ounces from photovoltaic demand. The analysis argues the net deficit is being sustained — and potentially deepened — by accelerating silver consumption in AI server interconnects, EV charging infrastructure, and medical applications, which together represent a demand stream less price-sensitive than solar. The practical implication is that the silver deficit's composition is shifting toward demand that is structurally stickier, reducing the probability that the current price correction is signalling a genuine demand slowdown.
